report:
The proposed construction meets the literal original P15.2 requirements, with its retained data and stated path hypotheses. This conclusion follows from reconstructing n1–n4 and checking their published foundations; earlier verdicts, partial labels, hashes and compilation play no mathematical role.

The controlling original wording is: “Construct a path-independent zero-volume Monge–Ampère theory with its carrier, dimension, mass and reference choices explicitly stated.” Section 9.2 requires: “Name the reference scale, dimensional carrier and retained singularity data, then prove independence of all claimed perturbation choices.” Problem 9.1 supplies the minimum-reference requirement: “After choosing the minimum necessary reference scale, is there a path-independent unnormalized energy and Monge–Ampère theory for a pseudoeffective zero-volume class?” P15.2 further states that “A family of perturbative probability measures is not automatically a canonical limiting operator, and raw mass cannot be recovered from I-equivalence alone.”

These sentences permit an explicitly reference-dependent theory on the geometric carrier X, whose complex dimension is n. They do not require a carrier of dimension d, identification with numerical dimension, or a geometric classification of reference equivalence. The explicit lower-dimensional numerical requirement belongs to P15.3. The discussion of an attempted class-volume-coefficient construction describes a route; it does not prescribe that route for P15.2. Likewise, “all claimed perturbation choices” requires proving the asserted path classes, rather than continuity along every conceivable varying-background approximation. Thus the ambient carrier is admissible here. The quotient W/N remains an operator-reference quotient; it is not an independently geometric construction or a geometric carrier.

Degree and vanishing check. The reference polynomial is the mass of the actual positive current P+εΩ, by positive-current multilinearity. Its class is big because this current dominates εΩ. Comparing its potential with a minimal-singularity potential bounds its top mass by vol(α+ε[Ω]), which tends to zero. Since every polynomial summand is nonnegative, M_n=0. M_0>0 consequently gives 0≤d<n. Pointwise comparison of two Kähler forms preserves positivity of every trace mass. DDNL bounded-type equality preserves these masses under reference-anchor changes. Slotwise monotonicity, completed with smooth Kähler slots, bounds each more-singular degree-k mixed mass by M_k. For k>d it vanishes; positivity and coefficient control by Kähler trace then force the current itself to vanish. None of this identifies d with numerical dimension.

Common-domain check. For D=Cω_0−ω_1 Kähler, each scalar deficit Δ_j is nonnegative: DDNL applies to exactly d potential slots and m smooth slots, all in pseudoeffective backgrounds. Expanding (ω_1+D)^m=C^mω_0^m gives a positive-coefficient sum of these deficits equal to zero. Hence every deficit vanishes, including the ω_1^m deficit. This proves auxiliary independence without asserting positivity of a difference of product currents. At d=0 both products are 1 and the condition is automatic. Pointwise comparison of complementary powers similarly preserves finiteness of every nonnegative joint-linear integral, including infinite integrals.

Vu’s relative-domain hypotheses are satisfied with d repeated reference slots and smooth relative current ω^m. Connectedness makes top-degree cohomology equality equivalent to mass equality. With source potentials u/2 and ψ/2, the diagonal source linear energy is (d/2) times the displayed binomial sum. Constant adjustments affect integrals only by finite mixed masses. The linear weight satisfies the source weight conditions. Convexity and bounded-equivalent reference invariance therefore apply. Averaging any finite family of full-mass inputs gives a full-mass diagonal product. Its positive expansion averages mixed masses each bounded above by the reference mass; equality of the average forces equality of every mixed mass. This establishes the mixed full-mass assertion used subsequently.

Bare-current convergence check. The capacity argument first applies GZ Proposition 3.7 to bounded truncations in a dominating Kähler background. Proposition 3.6 removes the unbounded sublevel tail; local/global capacity comparison and quasicontinuity justify the local bounded applications. For fixed K, b_K is bounded and quasicontinuous, and its nonzero locus lies in every strict truncation locus. All product factors used in DDNL Proposition 2.2 are uniformly bounded. Appending constant positive forms and decomposing complementary test forms legitimately obtains convergence against every complementary smooth test form. Increasing K then gives lower semicontinuity against weakly positive tests. This reconstructs the needed constant-background specialization of Vu’s lemma independently of its defective index notation.

Uniform trace mass supplies coefficient-measure compactness. Local potentials decrease and converge in L¹_loc, so every cluster current S dominates the target product. Their trace masses agree by the mixed full-mass result. The positive difference therefore has zero trace and vanishes. This proves the diagonal and mixed bare-current convergence, rather than merely convergence of one trace measure. Bounded-type truncations decrease to each full-mass input and give its actual product. Real truncation levels and other decreasing full-mass approximations are covered. The full-mass-limit hypothesis is essential and remains explicit.

Reference quotient check. Smooth multiplication defines L_u on actual forms independently of presentations. Bare-current truncation proves that the bounded-family kernel N is also the kernel on the entire full-mass domain. Consequently quotient equality is necessary and sufficient for equality of the whole fixed-type operator family. The factorization claim follows from ker(r)⊂N; it proves minimum sufficient reference data for this specified family, including its admissible powers. It asserts no universal minimum across all possible theories. This formal minimality is supplemented by the substantive common-domain and kernel-extension proofs, rather than presented as geometric classification.

The coefficient/trace estimate gives the uniform total-variation bound Q3. Taking the infimum over N proves Q4 and nondegeneracy of ρ; completeness is unnecessary. Combining Q4 with bare-current convergence proves the stated joint decreasing-input/quotient-data continuity. Polarization on the positive parameter cone and simultaneous truncation establish the mixed kernel characterization. The raw mass functional descends to the quotient, is positive on admissible powers, and equals the homogeneous cohomological pairing of the actual reference product. Bounded-equivalent anchor changes and simultaneous smooth θ-gauge changes preserve the domains and family data. DGMS applies to the smooth, real, closed, cohomologically exact (1,1)-difference of backgrounds.

The examples check analytically. The radial potential has positive singular Hessian, vanishing boundary flux and finite weighted singular integral ∫t^(2a−2)dt for a<1/2, giving an actually unbounded finite-energy member. On P¹×P¹, positivity and ∫T∧A=[A]²=0 force every current in [A] to be horizontal. Hence N={η:A∧η=0}. Disjoint vertical bumps give infinitely many independent exact-form quotient classes. The cohomologous reference forms therefore produce distinct measures with equal mass. The logarithmic reference has divisor current with zero nonpluripolar part, so its degree is zero although the smooth reference has degree one. The stated Poincaré–Lelong normalization follows from Δlog|z|²=4πδ_0 and dd^c=Δ/(4π). These examples support the claimed distinctions and refute no fixed-datum assertion.

Perturbation check. In P2, positivity in the original background permits the exact expansion P3. Higher terms vanish. Each remaining unscaled mass is bounded by the reference class polynomial; convergence of auxiliary classes makes these bounds uniform. Thus the lower-degree remainder is O(ε_j) in total variation when d≥1 and absent when d=0. Quotient-data convergence and decreasing bare-current continuity identify the leading term. Every input and its limit remain in the full-mass domain. No o(ε_j) potential rate is used or needed in this theorem.

P4 has different antecedents. Both perturbed currents are positive, their potentials have the reference bounded type, and h is a bounded admissible dsh difference. The mixed relative currents are closed positive and have no pluripolar mass, so the scoped IBP and association formulas apply. The correct gradient identity is ½dd^c(h²)∧R−h dd^ch∧R. The corrected cutoff estimate gives gradient mass O(1/k), and Cauchy–Schwarz removes boundary terms. DDNL bounded-type equality with one smooth auxiliary slot gives the polynomial of order ε^(m−1). Smooth auxiliary convergence makes the test constants uniform. After rescaling the error is O_f(δ_ε/ε), so δ_ε=o(ε) suffices. Uniform rescaled masses extend smooth-test convergence to continuous tests. The n=1,d=0 empty-product case is valid. Neither this proof nor P2 establishes unrestricted perturbed-background convergence, and the synthesis makes no such assertion.

The operator exists directly for every input in the common full-mass domain; conditional approximation theorems are not being used as its definition. Its carrier is X, its geometric dimension is n, its current bidegree is (d,d), and its positive raw mass is retained without probability normalization or I-only recovery. The minimum reference equivalence is proved for its entire family. These facts satisfy the genuine literal requirements identified above.

Harmless wording corrections are explicit: older supporting references to the cutoff’s “support” must mean its nonzero locus; older source-energy expressions require the factor d/2 in Vu’s convention. The submitted n1–n4 already contain these corrections. An older unbounded-factor invocation of Vu Theorem 3.3 cannot itself justify convergence; the submitted bounded-truncation reconstruction supplies the required application. Printed missing half factors and malformed convention extraction are not used as definitions. No substantial repair of n1–n4 is needed.

The supplied standing setup is connected. If disconnected manifolds are admitted, compactness gives finitely many components. The offered separate construction uses componentwise full-mass conditions, degrees, reference quotients and rescalings, then adds the measures. Different component degrees do not require equality or a single common perturbation exponent. No additional compatibility is needed for that explicitly componentwise theory.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-fold, the nonpluripolar product of 1≤p≤n closed positive (1,1)-currents is a finite closed positive (p,p)-current. It is symmetric, multilinear on positive sums, depends only on the currents, is plurifinely local, has no pluripolar trace mass, and commutes with smooth positive factors. BEGZ, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6, Theorem 1.8 ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2)).
passages.quote: is local in the plurifine topology whenever well-defined.

passages.statement: Every pseudoeffective real (1,1)-class on a compact Kähler manifold admits positive currents with minimal singularities, less singular than every positive current in that class. In a big class β their top nonpluripolar mass is vol(β). For pseudoeffective α and Kähler λ, vol(α+ελ) tends to vol(α) as ε decreases to zero. Positive products of nef classes equal their cup products. BEGZ, Sections 1.3–1.4 and Definition 1.17 ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2)).

Let X be a compact Kähler n-fold, θ_j smooth closed real (1,1)-forms with pseudoeffective classes, and u_j,v_j∈PSH(X,θ_j), for 1≤j≤n. If corresponding potentials have the same bounded singularity type, their top mixed nonpluripolar masses are equal. If every u_j is less singular than v_j, the u-tuple mass is at least the v-tuple mass. DDNL, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.4 ([primary paper](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf)).

For a compact Kähler n-fold X, a pseudoeffective class α, a closed positive reference P∈α, a smooth closed positive relative current R of bidegree (n−r,n−r), and 1≤r≤n, the diagonal relative full-mass space {T∈α:T is more singular than P and {⟨T^r⋅R⟩}={⟨P^r⋅R⟩}} and its joint-linear-energy subclass are convex. Writing T=θ+dd^c_su and P=θ+dd^c_sφ, the subclass is characterized by finiteness of Σ_a binom(r,a)∫(φ−u)⟨T^aP^(r−a)⋅R⟩ after u≤φ. It is unchanged by a cohomologous bounded-equivalent reference change. Vu, Corollary 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3)).

On an open subset of C^n, let each of n sequences of uniformly bounded psh functions converge in capacity to its psh limit. Let uniformly bounded quasicontinuous weights converge in capacity to a quasicontinuous limit. The weighted Bedford–Taylor top products converge weakly to the corresponding weighted limit product. DDNL, Proposition 2.2 ([primary paper](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf)).

On a compact Kähler n-fold with Kähler form Ω, bounded Ω-psh functions decreasing to a bounded Ω-psh limit converge in Cap_Ω. For negative Ω-psh v, Cap_Ω({v<−t})≤t^−1(∫(−v)Ω^n+n∫Ω^n). Ω-psh functions are quasicontinuous, and global Kähler capacity is comparable with local Bedford–Taylor capacities on relatively compact coordinate pieces. Guedj–Zeriahi, Propositions 3.6, 3.7 and 3.10, Corollary 3.8 ([primary paper](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/JGA05.pdf)).

On compact Kähler X, let R be closed positive of bidegree (n−1,n−1), and let h,f be bounded R-admissible dsh functions whose quasi-psh representation poles have zero R-mass. Their intrinsic signed relative products and finite gradients exist, diagonal gradients are positive, and ∫f⟨dd^c_sh⋅R⟩=∫h⟨dd^c_sf⋅R⟩=−∫⟨df∧d^c_sh⋅R⟩. For bounded quasi-psh differences the diagonal gradient is ½dd^c_s(h²)∧R−h dd^c_sh∧R. Iterated relative products associate. Vu, Proposition 2.1(iii), Equation (2.3), Lemmas 2.5–2.6 and Theorem 2.7 ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3)).

Let p_i,l≥p_i be psh functions on U⊂C^n converging to p_i in L¹_loc, with the relevant nonpluripolar products locally finite. With constant relative background R_l=R=1, for every compactly supported smooth weakly positive complementary form Φ, liminf_l∫⟨∧_i dd^cp_i,l⟩Φ≥∫⟨∧_i dd^cp_i⟩Φ. Constant backgrounds satisfy Condition (*), and the relative product with background 1 is the ordinary nonpluripolar product. Vu, Condition (*), Definition 3.3 and Lemma 4.1(i) ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11111v1)).
passages.quote: every smooth weakly positive form Φ with compact support in U

Vu’s source convention is d^c_s=i(∂̄−∂)/(2π) and dd^c_s=i∂∂̄/π. Vu, Notation and convention ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11111v1)).

On a compact Kähler manifold, every smooth d-closed, d^c-closed, d-exact form is dd^c-exact, over both the real and complex numbers. In particular, cohomologous smooth closed real (1,1)-forms differ by dd^c of a smooth real function, with scalar adjustment for the chosen convention. DGMS, Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.14 ([primary paper](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~dennis/publications/PDF/DS-pub-0024.pdf)).
passages.quote: This lemma holds for real as well as complex forms
